summary: Slice 1 of 3 (R1 finish). I read the earlier run's work on this branch and checked it against the requirements and design. The defaults map (47 entries), the SemanticType union, the icon registry, ZestIcon, the UI/index.ts exports, the .zestIcon styles and package.json (1.7.0) already match, so I changed no production code. I ran the four slice test files (semanticTypeIcons, ZestIcon, zestIconPerformance, semanticTypeButtonConfigDefaults) with coverage off; Jest also picked up 10 more suites that match those names. All 14 suites and 163 tests pass. I did not run the full suite with coverage, the build or a bundle-size check, and I did not read the docs/guidelines files that AGENTS.md lists. The tests below prove R1: all 47 types render an icon and keep their label, the 28 new names are accepted by SemanticType, a custom registration for a new name wins, unknown or differently-cased names render a plain button, and the defaults map lists every built-in name in its original order. Slice 2 verified against the code. The tests, docs and code already on the branch cover R2, R4, R5, R6, R7 and R8, and all of them pass. Added one test for the one gap found, the R2 pitfall that defaults must not edit the configuration the app passes in: a deeply frozen provider config is merged with the built-in defaults, the app's override wins for 'search', 'copy' keeps its built-in look, and neither the config nor the built-in map changes. No production code was changed. Result: 18 suites, 226 tests pass when run on __tests__ only. A plain `npx jest` also picks up old scratch copies of tests under .devteam/runs/20261025-084314/scratch, and 3 of those fail; they are not project tests. Slice 3 (DevelopmentDocs, BreakingChangesDocs, Readme) was already in place from the earlier attempt and checked against the code: README.md lists 47 types and ZestIcon with links to features/api/examples; documentation/development.md describes zestIcons.tsx and ZestIcon.tsx and says 47 types; documentation/breaking-changes.md records the Font Awesome to library-SVG icon change as visual with an additive API; Previous/Next links are present on every page; no '17 built-in types' wording remains. No source edits were needed this step. npm run build succeeds. The jest run shows 82 suites passing and 1005 tests passing; the only 3 failures are in stale copies under .devteam/runs/20261025-084314/scratch (not project files).

tests.name: R1: all 47 built-in types render a default icon and keep their children label
R1: each of the 28 new names is accepted by the SemanticType type
R1: an app that registered a custom configuration for a new name keeps its own configuration
R1: an unknown semanticType renders a plain button without an icon
R1: a name in capitals or with spaces is not treated as a built-in type
R1: lists all 47 built-in names and every one has a defaults entry
R1: keeps the 19 existing entries in their original order before the new ones
R2: every new type resolves to its documented variant and icon side
R2: no new type asks for confirmation by default
R2: a developer-supplied iconLeft wins and the default icon is not added twice
R2: a developer-set variant wins over the built-in default
R2: next places its icon after the label so right-to-left layouts mirror it
R3: every built-in type renders its icon in the shared style
R3: the icon box is sized in rem/em so it follows the small, medium and large button sizes
R3: a disabled button dims the icon with the text instead of leaving it at full strength
R3: an icon on a filled success or danger variant stays readable against the background
R3: the busy state shows its spinner instead of the type icon
R3: the success state shows its own check mark instead of the type icon
R3: the fail state shows its own cross instead of the type icon
R4: every built-in icon is hidden from screen readers and not focusable
R4: a built-in type with text children has an accessible name equal to that text
R4: an icon-only button with aria-label announces that label, not the icon
R4: every built-in type gets the shared keyboard focus ring in light and dark themes
R8: an icon added later without the shared view box or stroke settings fails the style test
R8: no icon carries a script, event handler, external link, image or raw HTML
R2: a frozen provider config and the built-in defaults are left untouched after rendering
R2: the 28 new types keep the documented variant and icon side
R2: only the eight async new types get a 500 ms busy time and none ask for confirmation
R5: renders the named built-in icon in the shared style
R5: an icon passed as iconLeft renders exactly one icon
R5: an unknown name renders nothing and does not throw
R5: the public barrel exports ZestIcon, its types, the default button, the provider and the config hook
R5: two ZestIcons on one page do not clash (no shared ids)
R5: a rem size or a size name scales the icon without px
R8: every built-in icon uses the shared view box and stroke settings
R7: the features table lists exactly the built-in semantic types
R7: the docs use the new types and icon component, with no stale type count
R7: every documentation page links to the previous and next page
R3: a hundred built-in buttons render one icon each and keep the module-level elements on re-render
R3: an icon element is created once and the same reference is reused on every lookup
R8: the icon registry is a fixed module-level map, not something rebuilt per render
R6: the 19 existing types keep their variant, button style, icon side and options
R6: the 19 existing names keep their variant, button style, icon side and label
R6: an iconLeft override from the provider wins for a built-in type
R8: the characterisation relies on the shared icon element, not on path data
R6: a provider override of a built-in type's iconLeft keeps the app's own icon
R6 and R8: a new type icon and the toggle check coexist without replacing each other
